Welcome to Hinchley Wood School
Welcome to the Hinchley Wood School website; we hope you find it useful and informative and that it gives you some sense of the school's vitality, values and the many achievements of our students. We are a state funded, non-selective 11-18 mixed comprehensive Academy. Our core business is teaching and learning and we have a relentless focus on teaching lessons of the highest quality - lessons that stimulate and inspire young minds. We do hope you enjoy this opportunity to learn more about our school and what makes Hinchley Wood such an outstanding learning community. Maria Cachia and Lucy Macdonald - Headteachers

Parent Partnership Policy
At the end of 2025, we updated our Parent Partnership Policy which you will find below.
Over the course of the last 12 months, we have reviewed the old Parent ‘Codes of Conduct’ and with the help of teachers, parents/carers, Local Governors and Trustees, we have produced an updated HWLP Parent Partnership Policy.
In creating this new Trust-wide approach to working in partnership with parents/carers we have enlisted the help of the UK’s biggest parent charity ‘Parentkind’. We will be working alongside them over the course of this new year as we recognise how important it is to have positive parent-school partnerships both for the wellbeing and academic progress of our children.
Our recent Trust INSET day in November 2025 was dedicated to this topic and the whole staff body was involved in looking at strategies to further support communication and relationships.

Fantastic A Level results - school records broken!
A level Exam Results 2026
A huge well done to our Year 13 students for achieving absolutely fantastic A level results, and breaking school records! The Sixth Form area was full of celebration this morning with students congratulating each other, alongside staff, parents and carers. We knew they were a special year group and we are delighted that their hard work has paid off, with the vast majority now arranging their university accommodation.
Our headline A Level results are:
A few individuals to highlight are:
At the time of writing, 85 students have secured their first choice place and 13 students have secured their insurance place in a wide range of subjects, from medicine to business management to psychology. Three students are off to study at Oxbridge; James (History) and Annabel (Biology) at Oxford, and Josh (Economics) at Cambridge.
These outstanding results reflect the hard work and resilience of our students, as well as the dedication and expertise of our talented teachers, and the excellent pastoral care and support from our fantastic Sixth Form Team, led by Miss Gray and Mrs Brown.
“Wow. What an exceptional set of results for an exceptional year group. We could not be prouder of our Year 13 students and all that they have achieved. These results are a wonderful reflection of the incredible hard work, determination and resilience they have shown throughout their time with us.
This has been a particularly special year group, and one that will hold a very special place in our hearts. They have been an outstanding group of young people: talented, kind, ambitious and full of character. We have loved watching them grow, develop and flourish, and we feel incredibly privileged to have shared their journey with them.
As I said at their leavers’ assembly, it has been a genuine privilege to work alongside such an extraordinary group. They have made us laugh, challenged us, inspired us and, quite simply, made their mark on our school. We may not be supposed to have favourites, but if we did… this year group would certainly be very high on the list!
We know how much effort has gone into achieving these results, and we hope every single student takes a moment to recognise just how much they have accomplished. They should be immensely proud of themselves.
A huge congratulations to all of our Year 13 students. We wish them every happiness and success as they take their next steps, whether that is university, an apprenticeship, employment, travel or another exciting new adventure.
We will miss them enormously, but we hope they will keep in touch and remember that they will always be part of our school community. Well done, Year 13. You have made us incredibly proud.”
Miss Gray – Head of Year 13 and Co-Head of Sixth Form
Josh H with 4A*s

Fantastic GCSE Results at Hinchley Wood School!
Fantastic GCSE Results at Hinchley Wood School!
We are delighted to announce another year of exceptional GCSE results with students achieving academic success across the board. The year group have set a new school record at Grade 9, with 250 Grade 9s achieved by this cohort, representing 16% of all grades.
There are so many fantastic headlines:
· 16% of all grades are Grade 9,
· 32% of all grades are Grade 8 or 9
· 47% of all grades are Grade 7 and above (22% nationally)
· 89% of students achieved 5 or more GCSEs at Grade 4 or above
· 86% of students achieved 5 or more GCSEs including English and Maths.
· 90% of all grades are at Grade 4 or above (67% nationally)
Some amazing individual achievements include:
· Lily D, Jaemani G, Gemma M, and Sam S achieved eight Grade 9s and one Grade 8
· Artie N and Leo U achieved eight Grade 9s
· Kush C, Eleanor D, Jude G, Amy L, Nate M achieved seven grade 9s
“We are incredibly proud of all our Year 11 students. Their resilience and commitment to their studies, and their embodiment of our school values, has been inspiring particularly over the last year. Whilst many students have achieved Grade 7s and above, some of the notable successes are amongst the students who have faced challenges, yet despite these, they have persevered to secure good GCSE passes and should be congratulated. We hope that all students have been set up with the vital foundations for future success”. Lucy Macdonald - Headteacher
“What a fantastic morning celebrating the students’ excellent GCSE results. It was so lovely to share in their special morning, and celebrate with them after all their revision and hard work. We are delighted that so many are enrolling to study A levels here, and we wish all students moving to a different provider all the best in the future and hope they stay in touch with the school. ” Miss Cheney - Pastoral Lead
We would also like to acknowledge and thank the exceptional commitment the staff body have given to this year group over the last five years, and especially last year. Their unrelenting commitment, and going the extra mile for these students has significantly contributed to these fantastic results. We would also like to thank parents and carers for your unwavering support – it really has been a team effort.
Congratulations to our Year 11 students on such GCSE brilliant results; you really have made the whole school community proud!

The Hinchley Wood Super Curriculum aims to inspire students to delve deeper into their subjects, offering a range of opportunities and suggested activities to extend and challenge their thinking, knowledge, and skills.
This page contains a range of self-directed activities for each subject. These are activities that are linked to the curriculum but encourage students to go above and beyond the classroom and are completed in students’ own time. Each subject’s page is broken down by key stage and split into read/watch/listen/visit/create/explore.
The ideas provided are designed to immerse students in the wider context of each subject, providing them with greater insight into what the subject entails and nurturing their enthusiasm for learning. We hope that any interested student will take up some of the ideas offered.

Year 12 Futures Evening 2026 - Tuesday 3rd March 2026 It was wonderful to welcome so many parents and carers to our Futures Evening for 2027 applications, featuring guidance on applying to university and apprenticeships. Slides from the evening can be viewed below. It includes a step-by-step guide on applying to university via UCAS, comparing courses using Unifrog, and preparing personal statements. It outlines key deadlines, open days, and financial considerations such as tuition fees. It features helpful information exploring degree apprenticeships, their benefits, and application processes. Additionally, it provides resources for researching career options, work experience, and university financial planning. Futures Evening Presentation 2026 For further information, please contact Futures and Careers Coordinator, Robyn Boyd rboyd@hinchleywoodschool.co.uk.
Parental support has always been central to the success of Hinchley Wood School. Over the years, the time, skills, experience, and connections generously shared by many parents have made an invaluable contribution to enriching the life of the school and opportunities for the students.
If you can provide valuable careers experience to our students please submit your details in this form and we will come back to you.
Apprenticeships
Apprenticeships are an excellent alternative to University; apprentices are paid from day one and have work experience in the career of their choice, as well as studying for a qualification up to, and including, degree level. 2026 Work Experience Week: 29th June - 3rd July.
Year 12 students are expected to undertake a work experience placement during the summer term. Students are encouraged to find their own work experience placements, they are supported to do so by the Futures and Careers Coordinator, who also holds a bank of industry contacts that can be utilised if needed. Work Experience - What is it and Where to Find It? Work Experience - How to Contact Employers
Oxbridge Programme
Hinchley Wood Sixth Form runs a comprehensive Oxbridge Programme for Years 12 and 13.
Students with the relevant academic profile are invited to join the Oxbridge Group in Year 12. The group meets fortnightly to:
OMS (Oxford Mentoring Scheme) is an online mentoring scheme which all candidates are encouraged to apply for. This provides regular online meetings with a current Oxford Undergraduate in the students’ specialist subject and 2 or 3 students from other schools. The Undergrad facilitates discussions, sets tasks and answers questions on the academic subject, admissions process and interviews.
Mock interviews are undertaken with all candidates often including external subject experts.
Enrichment Tutorials are offered to applicants from the group covering 8 weekly sessions delivered by two Oxford graduates on the history of thought, from The Enlightenment to Postmodernism, and include consideration of politics, art, literature, music and philosophy, culminating with an individual tutorial.
Subject Specialist Tutorials are offered by teachers at the school and replicate Oxbridge tutorials and interviews, challenging students to question and think more deeply about their chosen subject.
For more information on this please contact Dr. Caroline Whitehouse, Oxbridge Coordinator, CWhitehouse@hinchleywoodschool.co.uk
Practice past entrance exam papers.
Partnership with Procter & Gamble
Headstart Programme for Year 12
In Year 12, students are invited to participate in a project called the 'Headstart Programme' with multinational company Procter and Gamble, where they will step into the role of a P&G sales team launching an exciting new product. As part of this challenge, they will choose a retailer to pitch their product to and have a £1 million budget to plan the launch.
Throughout the project, they will develop key skills in finance, marketing, and sales, guided by industry insights. Creativity is strongly encouraged, alongside strategic thinking.
At the end of the project, students will deliver a 7-10 minute presentation, ensuring that each team member contributes. They will also take part in a 5-minute Q&A session to showcase their understanding and ability to respond to challenges. P&G then announces winners and gives out a small prize to those who have won. Corporate Breakfast with P&G Degree Apprentices
In Sixth Form, we host three corporate breakfast events each year, one of which is held in partnership with Procter & Gamble. During this event, P&G apprentices and staff join our students for an informal breakfast and conversation. This provides our sixth formers with the opportunity to ask questions, gain insights into careers at P&G, and explore potential pathways. In turn, P&G can share information about their degree apprenticeship program and connect with potential future applicants.
For more information on this partnership please contact Robyn Boyd, rboyd@hinchleywoodschool.co.uk

Rewarding Students Who Give Back
At the beginning of the academic year, Year 10 students were encouraged to embrace a vision of giving back to both the school and the wider community. We are delighted to celebrate the many students who have done exactly that, demonstrating a wonderful commitment to service, leadership and community spirit throughout the year.
Students have contributed to school life in a wide range of ways. Many applied to become Student Ambassadors and represented the school at key events such as Open Evening and Parents' Evenings, helping prospective families and visitors gain an insight into life at Hinchley Wood School. Others have supported the Remembrance Service, acted as buddies for new students joining the school, spoken with university researchers, and even contributed to discussions with local MP Monica Harding on the important topic of mobile phones and teenagers.
These opportunities have allowed students to develop confidence, responsibility and leadership skills while making a meaningful contribution to the school community. Their willingness to volunteer their time and support others reflects the values we are proud to promote at Hinchley Wood School.
To congratulate all of the students who have participated in these activities throughout the year and their positive contribution, they were invited to take part in a Colour Run – a well-deserved reward and celebration of their efforts.

Overview for Students, Teachers, Employers, Parents/Carers and Governors
Hinchley Wood School is dedicated to providing students with high-quality career learning opportunities aligned with the Gatsby Benchmarks, ensuring a comprehensive and effective careers education throughout their time with us. We recognise that all young people need guidance to navigate their educational journey and prepare for adult life. Our students benefit from a carefully planned programme of activities designed to help them make informed decisions, choose appropriate 14-19 pathways, and plan their careers both during school and beyond.
Our careers programme integrates internal careers education with independent and impartial careers information, advice, and guidance (IAG) provided by external experts. We prioritise ensuring that every school leaver, whether at the end of Year 11 or Year 13, has a robust and suitable plan for their next steps.
Oversight of our careers programme is led by the Careers Lead and Head of Careers, who are responsible for implementing and monitoring its success. The programme aligns with all eight Gatsby Benchmarks, including addressing individual needs, embedding career learning in the curriculum, and linking curriculum learning to careers.
We collaborate with the Elmbridge 14-19 Consortium, Surrey County Council Careers Hub, and national and local businesses, colleges, and universities to enrich our careers education. Our strong alumni network and partnerships with parents and carers further enhance the support and advice available to students, helping them to succeed in their future pathways.
This newsletter is a collation of all the opportunities we have heard about from employers and universities. Please use the links included to read more information and apply to anything you are interested in. Links are underlined.

The CEIAG Policy below sets out the school’s approach to careers education. Our Provider Access Policy sets out the school’s arrangements for managing the access of providers to students and parents/carers at the school. Gatsby Benchmarks
The CEIAG provision at Hinchley Wood School is mapped against the eight Gatsby Benchmarks, which is reviewed annually by the Head of Careers.
Every school and college should have an embedded programme of career education and guidance that is known and understood by students, parents/carers, teachers and employers.
Every student and their parents/carers should have access to good-quality information about future study options and labour market opportunities. They will need the support of an informed adviser to make best use of available information.
Students have different career guidance needs at different stages. Opportunities for advice and support need to be tailored to the needs of each student. A school’s careers programme should embed equality and diversity considerations throughout.
All teachers should link curriculum learning with careers. For example, STEM subject teachers should highlight the relevance of STEM subjects for a wide range of future career paths.
Every student should have multiple opportunities to learn from employers about work, employment, and the skills that are valued in the workplace. This can be through a range of enrichment activities including visiting speakers, mentoring and enterprise schemes.
Every student should have first-hand experiences of the workplace through work visits, work shadowing and/or work experience to help their exploration of career opportunities, and expand their networks.
All students should understand the full range of learning opportunities that are available to them. This includes both academic and vocational routes and learning in schools, colleges, universities and in the workplace.
Every student should have opportunities for guidance interviews with a careers adviser, who could be internal (a member of school staff) or external, provided they are trained to an appropriate level. These should be available whenever significant study or career choices are being made. This should be expected for all students but should be timed to meet their individual needs.

Provider Access Legislation (PAL)
The Provider Access Legislation (PAL) is new guidance that is coming into force in January 2023. The updated Provider Access Legislation (PAL) specifies schools must provide at least six encounters for all their students:
The new legislation will become a key mechanism to further help learners understand and take-up, not just apprenticeships, but wider technical education options such as T-Levels and Higher Technical Qualifications.
In summary, all students at Hinchley Wood School have opportunities to learn about opportunities to access alternative routes to employment, including vocational qualifications and apprenticeships via readiness curriculum activities which include; drop-down days, assemblies, tutorials, Unifrog, STEPs, work experience and careers fairs. The provisions made at Hinchley Wood School are detailed in the Provider Access Policy.
CEIAG Programme
CEIAG begins in Year 7 and continues through to Year 13. The programme includes lessons based on career planning, self-evaluation, making decisions, economic well-being and employability skills and is delivered through the STEPs Careers Programme and Unifrog in PSHE lessons. Careers education for Years 7 - 13 is mainly delivered through the PSHE curriculum, consisting of a twenty-minute tutorial every week. In addition, students in Years 7 – 9 receive a biweekly one-hour lesson.
Unifrog
This online platform is well-used by students as it helps them make intelligent, well informed choices about their futures. Unifrog allows students to use data to decide which route to choose after school, help students avoid common decision-making mistakes and enable teachers to track where their students have got to in making their choices. Students can also compare individual university courses and apprenticeships, allowing them assess going to university alongside doing an apprenticeship. Parents are also given full access to Unifrog to enable their informed involvement in a choice which will shape their childrens’ lives.

Individual Careers Guidance
The school works with an external, independent careers adviser to support and enhance the careers education provided. Mrs Lyn Canning is our Elmbridge 14–19 Consortium Careers Adviser, working across four Elmbridge schools, and is available on site every Thursday. She conducts one-to-one careers meetings with students from a range of year groups.
From Year 10, students are booked an individual careers appointment with Mrs Canning. All SEND and Pupil Premium students are offered an appointment in Year 9, ahead of making their GCSE option choices. Other students may request an appointment themselves or be referred by their Head of Learning or Form Tutor.
Appointments are prioritised for Year 10 and Year 11 students who are seeking guidance on their next steps. Each meeting results in a personalised action plan, which is emailed to the student to support them in progressing their plans.
Students in Years 12 and 13 are also offered careers appointments and receive additional support from the Careers and Futures Coordinator and Careers Lead, Mrs Robyn Boyd, particularly with Apprenticeship and UCAS applications.
To arrange a careers appointment, please contact Mrs Robyn Boyd at rboyd@hinchleywoodschool.co.uk
Labour Market Information (LMI)
Labour Market Information (LMI) is a useful tool to help research future jobs in the local area, understand the skills needed for certain roles and the demand for future employment. It helps to break down the complex ‘world of work’, ranging from descriptions of different careers, their entry routes, promotional prospects, salaries paid, skills and qualifications needed, etc. Crucially for young people, LMI also covers future demand e.g. what kinds of jobs will be in demand after leaving school and what kinds of skills will be needed. As parents/carers you play a vital part in ensuring your child gains the best information, advice and guidance to prepare them for life once they leave Hinchley Wood School both with the skills they have developed and the knowledge they have.
